text.title: Freelancer Payment Chase Script Library Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every payment-chase ladder MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: The ladder MUST have exactly three rungs keyed to calendar days after the invoice due date (not the send date): polite at T+3, firm at T+10, legal-mention at T+30. Each rung's scheduled send date MUST be computed from the due date stated on the invoice and recorded in the artefact. A rung sent earlier than its clock, or two rungs collapsed into one message, is rejected.

rationale.source: Methodology design (AGENTS.md); widely established practice in freelance and small-business collections

rule.rationale: Clients who pay late are mostly disorganised, not malicious, and a firm message three days after the due date turns a slow payer into an ex-client. The clock is the relationship-preservation mechanism: it guarantees the polite assumption gets its chance before anything escalates, and it stops the freelancer from sending the legal rung in a moment of frustration on day 12.

rule.statement: Every rung MUST quote, verbatim from the source of record: invoice number, invoiced amount with currency, invoice date, due date, days overdue on the send date, and the payment-terms clause id from the contract. The invoice PDF or link MUST be attached or linked on every rung. A rung drafted from memory or with any of these fields blank is rejected.

rationale.source: Commercial-collections practice; small-claims filing requirements in most jurisdictions

rule.rationale: The accounts-payable person who reads the message has never seen the project; they need the invoice number to find it and the due date to justify paying it now. When the ladder is exhausted, the same six facts are what a collections agency or a small-claims form asks for, so getting them right on rung one is what makes rung three possible.

rule.statement: A rung MAY mention late interest, a fixed late fee, work suspension or withheld IP assignment ONLY when the contract clause or a statute grants it, and MUST quote the exact clause id or statutory basis and rate (UK business-to-business: Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998, statutory interest at 8% over the Bank of England base rate plus fixed compensation; EU: Directive 2011/7/EU). Inventing a fee, a rate or a consequence that appears in no contract or statute is forbidden.

rationale.source: Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 (UK); Directive 2011/7/EU on combating late payment in commercial transactions

rule.rationale: A made-up "5% weekly penalty" is unenforceable, hands the client a reason to dispute the whole invoice, and in some jurisdictions exposes the freelancer to a harassment complaint. A real clause quoted by number does the opposite: the client's finance team recognises it as a cost that grows and pays to stop it.

rule.statement: The T+3 rung MUST assume administrative oversight: no blame language, no mention of fees, suspension or legal steps, the invoice attached, and exactly one question asking for a confirmed payment date. It MUST be sent to the same recipient who received the invoice. Message length MUST NOT exceed 120 words.

rationale.source: Methodology relationship-preservation goal; widely established practice in collections communication

rule.rationale: Most three-day-late invoices are stuck in an approval queue or a wrong inbox. The message that gets paid fastest is the one that is easiest to forward to finance with "please sort this". Anything that reads as a complaint has to be answered rather than forwarded, and answering takes longer than paying.

rule.statement: The T+10 rung MUST state a specific pay-by date no more than 7 days after the send date, name the single consequence that follows from the contract (per r-fees-and-leverage-only-from-contract-or-statute) if the date passes, and add the client's accounts-payable or finance contact to the recipients alongside the original sponsor. It MUST NOT threaten legal action or a collections agency.
rule.rationale: A firm message with no date is a polite message with a worse tone. The date creates the decision point; the named consequence makes it credible; copying finance removes the sponsor as a bottleneck. Mentioning lawyers on rung two burns the legal rung's credibility and the relationship at the same time.

rule.statement: The T+30 rung MUST be a formal notice: full legal names and addresses of both parties, the invoice ledger with the outstanding total including any contractual or statutory interest, a final deadline of 7 to 14 days, the specific next step (collections agency, small-claims or county-court claim, statutory demand where applicable) and a statement that the notice is sent without prejudice to the relationship. It MUST be sent by email and by the written-notice channel the contract names (registered post where required), and MUST NOT be sent before rungs one and two are logged.

rationale.source: UK Practice Direction on Pre-Action Conduct and Protocols (letter before claim); comparable pre-action expectations in small-claims procedure elsewhere

rule.rationale: Courts and collections agencies expect to see a clear final demand before a claim, and a client's lawyer will look for one. A vague "we may have to take further steps" does not qualify. The formal shape is also what makes the client take it seriously: a letter that looks like a claim gets routed to someone with authority to pay.

rule.statement: The ladder MUST halt immediately when (a) payment is received in full, (b) the client raises a written dispute about the invoice or the work, which routes to dispute handling rather than the next rung, or (c) the legal rung's final deadline has passed, which routes to the named legal or collections handoff. On partial payment the outstanding balance MUST be recomputed and every subsequent rung MUST state the new balance. Sending the next rung after any of these events is forbidden.
rule.rationale: A firm chase sent the morning after payment landed is the single most damaging message in the library. A chase sent to a client who has raised a genuine dispute converts a fixable disagreement into a standoff. And a ladder that never hands off means the freelancer keeps sending rung three, which teaches the client it is empty.

rule.statement: Every send MUST be logged with invoice id, rung, send date, channel, recipients, and the client's response (date and gist, or "none"). The log MUST yield days-to-pay per client per invoice, and at contract renewal the artefact MUST state the resulting change to terms for that client (shorter net terms, deposit, milestone billing, or none) with the log as evidence.

rationale.source: Methodology design: log send + response feeds contract re-audit; widely established credit-control practice

rule.rationale: Without the log the freelancer relitigates the same client's habits from memory every quarter and never changes the terms. With it, "this client averaged 41 days on net-15 across four invoices" is a sentence that justifies a 50% deposit at renewal, and the client cannot argue with their own payment history.
